title: Finite inseparable extension making a reduction geometrically reduced
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Assume that $Z$ has finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. There is a finite purely inseparable field extension $k\subseteq k\prime$ [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] such that $(Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k\prime)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] is geometrically reduced over $k\prime$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]: its base change to every field extension of $k\prime$ is reduced.

proof.text: For each irreducible component of Z choose its generic point using [lem-sc-scheme-sober], and let K_i be its residue field. The map k to the stalk of Spec k is a localization, the stalk map of f is essentially of finite type, and the residue map is a quotient; their composite is essentially of finite type. For fields this says that K_i/k is finitely generated. This works for Z itself, without first reducing Z.

Embed all the K_i into a finitely generated common field E/k by [lem-pur-finite-family-common-extension]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-make-separable] once to E/k. It gives a finite purely inseparable extension l/k and a field F with compatible maps k to l to F and k to E to F, where F/E is finite and F/l is separable. Since E/k is finitely generated and F/E finite, F/k and then F/l are finitely generated. Apply the definition [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] to the top intermediate field of F/l. By [lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-tensor-reduced], F tensor_l L is reduced for every field extension L/l. The affine pullback isomorphism then shows that Spec F is geometrically reduced over l.

Let P be the base change Z_l and Y its reduction. Each composite Spec F to Spec K_i to Z is compatible with Spec F to Spec l to Spec k, hence lifts to P. Since Spec F is reduced the lift factors through Y. The map q:Y to Z is a homeomorphism: its first factor is reduction, by [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism], and its second is purely inseparable field base change, by [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep]. Thus the lifted point maps to the chosen generic point in Z.

Take the coproduct W of one copy of Spec F for each irreducible component, and let g:W to Y be induced by the lifts. The image of q composed with g contains every generic point of Z. Every point of Z lies in an irreducible component and is a specialization of its generic point, so g has dense range because q is a homeomorphism. W has finitely many points; all its open subsets are quasi-compact, so g is quasi-compact. Y is reduced, hence [lemma-nagata-reduced-dense-image-schematic] makes g schematically dominant. No quasi-compactness assumption on Z is needed.

The finite coproduct W is geometrically reduced over l: after any field base change its coproduct open cover has reduced members, being the base changes of Spec F. Apply [lem-sbc-geometrically-reduced-dominant-descent] to the quasi-compact schematically dominant g:W→Y from the preceding step. It gives geometric reducedness of Y=(Z_l)_red directly. When Z is empty the family and coproduct are empty and the argument remains valid, with E=k.
